candidate.source_commit_boundary: Parent will freeze these exact bytes; no provisional Git commit is asserted by this review.

scope: Read the complete C5 changes to store.py and token_budget.py relative to C4, including follow-up guard fixes.
Read every new test in tests/test_round5_candidate_c5.py and independently recompute runtime and listed file hashes.

findings_fixed.problem: An original Encoding method rebound to another Encoding has the same __func__ but a different __self__. A warm count keyed to the first encoding could therefore be returned for a call that now uses the other encoding. The same function-only guard also allowed a counter method rebound to another counter to retain sealed-boundary certification.
findings_fixed.fix_verified: _ordinary_encoding now requires the original function and the exact bound receiver for counter.count, counter.count_after and all three Encoding methods.

findings_fixed.problem: Unconditional private _tiktoken import and direct _core_bpe access could reject a custom encoder whose original public exact-count method still worked.
findings_fixed.fix_verified: _encoding obtains the public encoder/version first, treats optional typed native-core inspection as certification only, and returns an uncertified fallback when private inspection is unavailable.

findings_fixed.identified_by: core implementation follow-up; independently checked here
findings_fixed.problem: Removing private Python pattern metadata after memo warming must disable the optimization without adding an AttributeError before an otherwise working original encode.
findings_fixed.fix_verified: _memo_identity uses tolerant getattr for the current pattern and requires identity with the previously approved immutable pattern.

reviewed_invariants: The original TokenCounter.count method owns the optional memo; no replacement wrapper changes its sealed-boundary method identity.

Eligible keys contain the complete unchanged native str and tokenizer name; a bounded current Encoding/CoreBPE identity map governs reuse. No page/query/result identity or normalized/digest-only text key is used.

Both registered tokenizer names share 2048 entries and 2097152 retained str-object bytes. sys.getsizeof is charged after successful encode; oversized values bypass storage without evicting normal entries.

Encoding/core/method/version/pattern changes bypass reuse and invalidate retained generations. The same core identity guard protects sealed-boundary certification; clearing the encoding loader cannot recertify a replaced private core.
Identity is checked again after a real encode before insertion. Zero counts remain valid hits and encode exceptions are not cached.
Subclass text and counters, class/instance wrappers, cross-receiver original methods, unknown implementations and missing private metadata retain original exact counting.
Memo allocation is lazy for token-budget recalls; character-only recall and nonallocating diagnostics leave it absent. Standalone counters do not receive a connection memo.
MemoryBook.close clears entries, text-byte accounting and retained encoder identities even if DB close and directory-cache cleanup raise.
All retrieval, corruption validation, source projection and full response assembly still execute. New warm-memo source-corruption and complete-payload differential tests cover that boundary.
test_evidence_boundary: The core agent reported its directed suite and dependency-free checks passed. This independent reviewer inspected the tests and changes but did not rerun or add those test counts. The parent retains the separate correctness execution receipt.
limits: A static review and small targeted regression suite do not prove every possible program execution.

The certification trusts the initially observed native tokenizer implementation. Deliberately forging the private tokenizer registry/core and matching metadata before first observation remains outside the pre-existing certification contract.
The 2 MiB bound covers retained text objects, not key/container/encoder overhead or whole-process memory. Actual RSS and the original independent resource-review gate still apply.

This verdict authorizes the next preregistered development comparison only. It is not numerical performance acceptance, a release approval, a new retrieval-quality evaluation or competitor superiority evidence. No v0.3.3 approved-runtime hash may be inferred from it.
